summary: Christopher Key Chapple is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982), Stony Brook University (attested 1983), and Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).

Christopher Minkowski (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard and the University of Delhi, and held posts at Brown, Cornell (1989–2006), and the University of Oxford as Boden Professor of Sanskrit (2005–2023).

Christopher Pinney (born 1959) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the Australian National University (~1993–1994) and University College London (from ~2000), along with positions at Chicago, Cape Town, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Northwestern.

Christopher S. George works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Royal W. Weiler in 1965, founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies (1972), and taught at IASWR (attested 1982).

Christopher S. Queen (born 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. His career includes posts at Harvard University as Dean of Students for Continuing Education (~1989) and Lecturer on Buddhism and World Religions (attested 2013).

Christopher Wallis is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Rochester, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt (PhD 2014). He guest lectured at Naropa University (attested 2020).

Chu-tsing Li (1920–2014) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa, teaching at Nanking (1943–1947), Iowa (~1955–1966), and the University of Kansas (from 1966).

Chun-i Tang (1909–1978) was a sinologist and philosopher who studied at National Central University, where he later taught (1944–1949). He co-founded The Chinese University of Hong Kong, serving as chair professor (1963–1974), and taught at New Asia Institute (~1949–1978).

Chun-min Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello (attested 2004), having also studied under Todd Brown, Chanyun, and Sheng Yen.

Chuta Ito (1867–1954) was a Japanese scholar of history and archaeology. Educated at the University of Tokyo (~1889–1892), he later held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1905–1928) and Waseda University (~1928–1937).

Chögyam Trungpa (1939–1987) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and teacher. He studied at Oxford (1963) and under teachers including Khenpo Gangshar. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1967), Naropa University (1973), Shambhala Training, and Gampo Abbey.

Chöje Akong Tulku Rinpoche (1939–2013) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1967, he founded Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre, where he later served as abbot (attested 2009).

Chökyi Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He was also a teacher to Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Chökyi Nyima is a scholar who pursued studies under the guidance of Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Chökyi Nyinche studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyaltsab, and later served as a teacher to Dilgo Khyentse.

Chönyi Drolma is a practitioner and scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Her education included studying under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).

Chüan-ying Yen specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University (attested 1986), where she studied under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, tutor Chu-tsing Li, and teacher John Hay.

Chün-fang Yü (born 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1965–1973) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen, later holding professorial posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University (~2001).

Clara Sue Kidwell (1941–2025) studied at the University of Oklahoma (PhD ~1970). A historian, she held posts at UC Berkeley (~1974–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian (~1993–1995), Oklahoma (1995), and UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).

Clare Carlisle (born 1977) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002) and held academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and King's College London (~2011).
